messages:
incident-bot: Pager: Elevated 5xx + latency spike for Hosted API in us-east-1 and several Dedicated pools (us-east-1). Error signature: auth token validation failures + upstream 502s from AWS managed auth service. Paging sara (on-call).

sara (on-call): I'm on it. seeing 5xx rate up ~13% for last 3m, median latency jumped from 80ms -> 680ms. Logs show repeated `token_validation_failed` and a bunch of `upstream: 502` from our auth proxy.

mike (sre): confirming CloudWatch metrics for us-east-1 show control-plane API throttling + ENI detach flaps around same timeframe. Could be an AWS regional issue impacting our auth provider endpoints too.

leo (eng-runtime): can we immediately fail-open auth for short-lived internal calls, and route external traffic to fallback region? I'll prepare a canary route.

sara (on-call): good idea. First: reduce blast radius. Steps:
- add routing override to prefer us-west-2 for new sessions
- increment dedicated pool scaling in other regions
- enable auth local cache fail-open for non-critical token checks
- throttle observability/ingest to reduce control-plane pressure

anita (product): priority: minimize customer-visible 5xx. Notify support + status page. I'll draft message for status page and the customer-facing slack channel.

cato (support): pinging largest affected customers now (enterprise customers tied to us-east-1 Dedicated). I'll include mitigation steps and ETA.

leo (eng-runtime): applying routing override:

```
# routing override snippet
route.preferred_regions = ["us-west-2","eu-west-1"]
route.fallback_policy = "reroute-on-5xx"
```

leo (eng-runtime): pushed config to edge router. New sessions should go to us-west-2. Existing pinned sessions in us-east-1 will still see errors until they reconnect.

mike (sre): scaling note: bumped dedicated pool autoscale min in us-west-2 by +20% and enabled burst. Also disabled a couple of non-essential control-plane tasks to free up API tokens.

observability-bot: WARNING: Log ingestion to observability vendor (thirdparty-logs) is delayed — retry queue length increased x3. Throttling ingest by 60% as per runbook.

sara (on-call): enabling auth fail-open for low-risk paths now (5 min patch):
```
auth.fail_open = true
auth.fail_open_whitelist = ["metrics","telemetry","non-customer-facing"]
```

sara (on-call): patched. Monitoring error rate.

mike (sre): AWS status page shows issue in us-east-1 for 'internal auth service endpoint' with degraded performance. We're seeing compounded failures: AWS endpoint throttles -> our auth provider token refreshes failing -> 502s back at API layer.

anita (product): status page update draft: "We're investigating elevated errors and latency in US East (us-east-1) affecting Hosted API and some Dedicated pools. Traffic is being routed to alternate regions; mitigation in progress. No data exfiltration. Updates every 15 minutes." Approve?

sara (on-call): approve, post.

cato (support): posted customer note and DM'd top 5 accounts. A few customers reported retrieval failures for background jobs — advising retry/backoff.

leo (eng-runtime): temporary mitigation reduced 5xx from 13% -> 4% overall. Latency median improved to ~220ms for routed traffic. Still seeing elevated errors for pinned sessions.

mike (sre): will open AWS support case with region-specific logs + request ETA. Also asked auth provider to increase token cache TTL temporarily.

observability-bot: we've paused high-cardinality traces and reduced span retention for us-east-1 to 30m to reduce ingestion. This will affect debug data but improve control-plane pressure.

sara (on-call): handing off to mike for longer-term mitigation. I'm going to sleep; i'm out at 02:20 UTC. Mike, you take post-patch investigation and customer timeline.

mike (sre): taking over. next steps:
- keep routing in place until AWS confirms resolution
- coordinate with infra to drain pinned sessions safely
- track customer incidents and close support loop
- collect detailed traces for RCA once stable

anita (product): PRD: coordinate a postmortem and a runbook update to include auth-provider token cache as a dependency. Also propose adding a proactive routing failover test in chaos infra.

cato (support): will keep customer channel open and send follow-ups as they request status.

mike (sre): AWS case opened (case# 123456789). Current impact summary for status/cs:
- regions affected: us-east-1
- services impacted: Hosted API, Dedicated pools pinned to us-east-1
- visible symptoms: elevated latency, ~4-13% 5xx (peak ~13%), token validation failures
- mitigation: region routing, auth fail-open for low-risk paths, scaled other-region capacity, throttled observability ingest

sara (on-call): thx all. If anything spikes again tag me, but mike has this.

mike (sre): scheduling checkin in 20m. will update thread and post final status when AWS confirms recovery or we finish migration.

observability-bot: NOTE: retention change applied for us-east-1 traces. Be aware for debugging window.

mike (sre): final update (1795101860): AWS reports partial recovery for affected endpoint. We're seeing error rates decline to baseline in us-east-1. Keeping routing override for 30m then slowly shift back. Preparing RCA ticket.

anita (product): thanks team — will coordinate postmortem and CS comms.
